question:
Statements: All scientists are researchers. All researchers publish papers.
Conclusion I: All scientists publish papers.
Conclusion II: Some paper publishers are researchers.
Which conclusions follow?
explanation: I follows by chain syllogism (All scientists→researchers→publish). II follows by converting 'All researchers publish papers' to 'Some paper publishers are researchers.' Both are valid.

question:
Statements: No pens are pencils. All pencils are stationery.
Conclusion I: No pens are stationery.
Conclusion II: Some stationery items are not pens.
Which conclusions follow?
explanation: I is wrong—pens may independently belong to stationery. II: all pencils are stationery and no pencil is a pen, so those pencil-stationery items are definitely not pens → some stationery items are not pens. Only II follows.

question: If a student scores above 80%, she receives an A grade. Sana scored 85%. What can we definitively conclude?

options.B: Sana may not have received an A grade

explanation: Modus Ponens: P→Q and P is true → Q is true. 85% > 80% (P), therefore Sana received an A grade (Q).

question: Rule: Only employees who submit all required forms receive their salary. Ahmed did not receive his salary. What can we conclude?

options.A: Ahmed did not submit all forms
options.B: Ahmed submitted all forms but was cheated
options.C: Ahmed is not a real employee

explanation: Contrapositive of 'submit all forms → receive salary' is 'did not receive salary → did not submit all forms.' Since Ahmed didn't receive his salary, he did not submit all forms.

question:
Argument: Reading fiction regularly improves empathy.
Which of the following most strengthens this argument?

options.A: A study of 500 adults found that those who read fiction scored 30% higher on empathy tests than non-readers.
options.B: Some people who never read fiction are very empathetic.
options.C: Fiction books often contain unrealistic scenarios.
options.D: Reading any book takes time away from socialising.

explanation: Direct empirical evidence linking fiction reading to measurably higher empathy scores provides the strongest support for the causal claim.

question:
Argument: We should install more streetlights in this neighbourhood to reduce crime.
Premise: Most crimes in this area happen at night.
What assumption is being made?

options.B: The neighbourhood has very high crime rates.
options.D: Night-time is when most people are asleep.

explanation: The argument jumps from 'crimes happen at night' to 'streetlights reduce crime.' The unstated link is the assumption that better lighting deters criminals.

question: A hospital that opened a new cardiac surgery unit saw its overall patient death rate increase. Which best explains this paradox?

options.A: The new unit attracted the most critically ill cardiac patients who had very high baseline mortality risk.
options.B: The surgeons in the new unit were poorly trained.
options.C: Death rates always increase in winter.

explanation: Selection bias: the new unit drew high-risk patients. Even with successful surgeries, complex cases carry high mortality, raising the hospital's overall death rate despite good relative outcomes.

question: In a class of 40 students: 20 passed Maths, 25 passed English, and 10 passed both. How many students passed at least one subject?
explanation: By inclusion-exclusion: |M ∪ E| = |M| + |E| − |M ∩ E| = 20 + 25 − 10 = 35 students.

question: Five books P, Q, R, S, T are placed on a shelf left to right. P is at the leftmost end. T is at the rightmost end. Q is immediately to the right of P. S is immediately to the left of T. Which book occupies the middle position?
explanation: Positions: 1=P, 2=Q (right of P), 5=T, 4=S (left of T). Position 3 must be R. R is in the middle.

question: A is the brother of B. B is the mother of C. What is A's relationship to C?
explanation: B is C's mother. A is B's brother, so A is the brother of C's mother → A is C's maternal uncle.

question: Pointing to a photograph, Tariq says, 'He is the son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the person in the photograph related to Tariq?
explanation: Tariq's grandfather's only son = Tariq's father. The son of Tariq's father = Tariq's brother. (If there are multiple sons of Tariq's grandfather, this could be a cousin, hence 'brother or cousin.')  In standard reasoning, the answer is brother.

question: Hina walks 6 km North, then turns right and walks 8 km East. What is the straight-line distance from her starting point?
explanation: Using Pythagoras: √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 km.

question: Farhan is facing West. He turns 90° clockwise, then another 90° clockwise. Which direction is he now facing?
explanation: Facing West → 90° clockwise = North → 90° clockwise = East. He now faces East.

question: In a code language, STAR is written as UVCT (each letter shifted +2). How is MOON coded?
explanation: Each letter +2: M→O, O→Q, O→Q, N→P. MOON = OQQP.

question: In a row of 25 students, Kamal is 7th from the left end. What is his position from the right end?
explanation: Position from right = Total − Position from left + 1 = 25 − 7 + 1 = 19th.

question: In a code language, WINTER is coded as ZLQWHU (each letter +3). How is FROST coded?
explanation: Each letter +3: F→I, R→U, O→R, S→V, T→W. FROST = IURVW.

question:
Statements: Some engineers are managers. All managers travel frequently. No frequent traveller owns a pet.
Conclusion I: Some engineers travel frequently.
Conclusion II: No manager owns a pet.
Which conclusions follow?
explanation: I: Some engineers are managers + all managers travel → some engineers travel ✓. II: All managers travel + no frequent traveller owns a pet → no manager owns a pet ✓. Both follow.

question:
Statements: All programmers know logic. Some logic experts win competitions. All competition winners receive trophies.
Conclusion I: Some programmers win competitions.
Conclusion II: Some logic experts receive trophies.
Which conclusions necessarily follow?
explanation: I: Cannot conclude — the logic experts who win competitions may not include any programmer. II: Some logic experts win + all winners receive trophies → some logic experts receive trophies ✓. Only II follows.

question: If it is a public holiday, the office is closed. If the office is closed, all employees stay home. Today is a national public holiday. What can we definitively conclude?

options.A: All employees are at home today.
options.B: Employees may or may not be at home.
options.D: Some employees may still come to the office.

explanation: Holiday → office closed (given); office closed → employees home (given). By chain: holiday → employees home. Today is a holiday, so all employees are home.

question: Rule 1: Only if a patient shows symptoms will the doctor run tests. Rule 2: Only if tests are run will the doctor prescribe medication. Adnan received medication. What can we conclude?

options.B: Adnan may not have shown symptoms.

explanation: Medication received → tests were run (contrapositive of Rule 2). Tests were run → symptoms showed (contrapositive of Rule 1). Therefore Adnan showed symptoms.

question:
Argument: The city's new recycling programme caused the 35% drop in landfill waste seen in its first year.
Which most strengthens this argument?

options.A: No other significant waste-reduction policies were implemented during the same period.
options.B: The city also banned single-use plastics at the same time.
options.C: Recycling programmes are generally expensive to run.
options.D: Citizens were not fully informed about the new programme.

explanation: Ruling out alternative explanations confirms the recycling programme—not other concurrent policies—caused the reduction, directly strengthening the causal claim.

question:
Argument: Increasing the minimum wage does not lead to increased unemployment.
Which most strengthens this argument?

options.A: Multiple large-scale studies found unemployment rates unchanged or slightly improved after minimum wage increases.
options.C: Business profits rose in the year following a minimum wage increase.
options.D: Economists frequently disagree about minimum wage effects.

explanation: Direct empirical evidence from multiple studies showing no unemployment increase after wage rises provides the strongest logical support.

question:
Argument: Dr. Saeed's new diet plan is healthy because it is endorsed by a famous celebrity.
Which most seriously WEAKENS this argument?

options.A: Celebrity endorsements are paid promotions and do not reflect medical expertise or clinical evidence.
options.B: The celebrity looks very fit and healthy.
options.C: Many people have tried the diet plan.
options.D: The diet plan was featured in a magazine.

explanation: A celebrity's opinion is not medical evidence (appeal to false authority). Pointing out that endorsements are paid promotions without clinical backing directly undermines the argument's reasoning.

question:
Argument: This university should ban smartphones in lecture halls to improve student performance.
Premise: Students retain 23% more information when not distracted by devices.
What underlying assumption is being made?

options.A: Smartphones in lecture halls are the primary source of distraction for students.
options.C: Banning items in general improves academic performance.
options.D: Lectures are the only place students use smartphones.

explanation: The argument assumes smartphones are the main distraction; otherwise banning smartphones would not address the core distraction problem and would not improve retention.

question:
Argument: Since Zara's bakery uses only organic ingredients, her cakes must be healthier than those of competing bakeries.
What underlying assumption is made?

options.A: Organic ingredients produce healthier food than non-organic alternatives.
options.B: Zara's cakes are more expensive than competitors'.
options.C: All competing bakeries use artificial preservatives.
options.D: Organic certification is difficult to obtain.

explanation: The conclusion 'healthier cakes' rests entirely on the unstated premise that organic ingredients are inherently healthier than non-organic ones.

question: A city introduced a congestion charge for cars entering the centre, yet traffic congestion worsened. Which best resolves this paradox?

options.A: The charge prompted commuters to drive alone at off-peak times instead of carpooling or using buses, increasing total vehicle trips.
options.B: Car prices fell significantly after the charge was introduced.
options.C: The congestion charge was set too high, causing public protests.
options.D: The city added more buses after the charge was introduced.

explanation: If commuters abandoned shared transport to make solo off-peak trips (avoiding the charge by timing), the total number of vehicle trips could rise, paradoxically worsening congestion.

question: Despite major advances in cancer treatment, the total number of cancer deaths in a country increased over the last decade. Which best explains this?

options.A: A significant increase in the elderly population meant more people were in the high-risk age group for cancer.
options.C: The government invested more in healthcare.
options.D: People began going for cancer screenings more regularly.

explanation: Better treatments may reduce case-fatality rates, but if the at-risk population (older people) grew substantially, absolute deaths can still rise—a demographic explanation for the paradox.

question:
A school recorded pass rates in four subjects over two years:
Maths: Year 1=60%, Year 2=78%
Physics: Year 1=55%, Year 2=70%
Chemistry: Year 1=70%, Year 2=65%
Biology: Year 1=65%, Year 2=72%
Which subject showed the greatest percentage-point improvement?
explanation: Improvements: Maths +18pp, Physics +15pp, Chemistry −5pp, Biology +7pp. Maths had the greatest improvement at 18 percentage points.

question: A store's daily sales for a week: Mon=120, Tue=90, Wed=150, Thu=80, Fri=200, Sat=250, Sun=110. On how many days did sales exceed the weekly average?
explanation: Total = 1000. Average = 1000/7 ≈ 143. Days exceeding 143: Wednesday (150), Friday (200), Saturday (250) — 3 days.

question:
Five people Ali, Bilal, Chaudhry, Dawood, Ehsan sit in a straight row facing south.
• Ali sits at the extreme left.
• Dawood is the immediate neighbour of both Ehsan and Chaudhry.
• Bilal is not at the extreme right.
• Ehsan is not adjacent to Ali.
What is Dawood's position from the left?
explanation: Ali=1. Ehsan not adjacent to Ali → Ehsan ≠ 2nd. Dawood flanked by Ehsan and Chaudhry. Valid arrangements: Ali-Bilal-Ehsan-Dawood-Chaudhry or Ali-Bilal-Chaudhry-Dawood-Ehsan. In both, Dawood is 4th from left.

question:
Six members—Grandfather(G), Grandmother(GM), Father(F), Mother(M), Son(S), Daughter(D)—sit for a photo.
• G and GM must sit together.
• F and M must sit at the extreme ends.
• S must not be adjacent to D.
Which arrangement is valid?

options.A: F, G, GM, S, D, M
options.B: F, S, G, GM, D, M
options.C: F, D, S, G, GM, M
options.D: M, G, GM, S, D, F

explanation: A: S(4) adjacent to D(5) ✗. B: F&M at ends ✓, G&GM together ✓, S(2) and D(5) not adjacent ✓. C: D(2) adjacent to S(3) ✗. D: S(4) adjacent to D(5) ✗. Only B satisfies all conditions.

question:
Six people—Amir, Bilal, Sana, Dina, Ehsan, Farida—sit around a circular table (6 seats, clockwise 1–6; opposites: 1↔4, 2↔5, 3↔6).
• Amir is at seat 1, opposite Bilal.
• Sana sits between Amir and Ehsan (seats 1-2-3).
• Dina sits opposite Ehsan.
Who sits between Bilal and Dina?
explanation: Amir=1, Sana=2, Ehsan=3, Bilal=4 (opp. Amir), Farida=5, Dina=6 (opp. Ehsan). Farida(5) sits between Bilal(4) and Dina(6).

question:
Four friends W, X, Y, Z sit around a square table, one per side.
• W and X do not sit opposite each other.
• Y sits immediately to W's right.
Who sits opposite W?
explanation: W at North. Y at East (right of W). W and X are not opposite, so X ≠ South. X must be at West. Z is at South, directly opposite W.

question: M is the sister of N. N is the brother of O. P is the father of N. Q is the husband of P's sister. How is Q related to O?
explanation: P is O's father (father of N, and N is O's brother, so P is parent of O). P's sister is O's paternal aunt. Q is the husband of P's sister → Q is O's paternal uncle (by marriage).

question: Uzma walks 5 km East, turns left and walks 3 km, turns left and walks 5 km, then turns left and walks 2 km. How far is she from the starting point and in which direction?
explanation: Start(0,0) → East 5=(5,0) → Left/North 3=(5,3) → Left/West 5=(0,3) → Left/South 2=(0,1). Distance from origin = 1 km due North.

question: In a class, Rida is ranked 15th from the top. Exactly 7 students are ranked between Rida and Nadia. If Nadia's rank is lower (higher number) than Rida's, what is Nadia's rank from the top?
explanation: Rida = 15th. 7 students between them, Nadia lower → Nadia = 15 + 7 + 1 = 23rd.

question:
Argument: Banning junk food advertisements during children's TV programmes will reduce childhood obesity.
Which most strengthens this?

options.A: Research shows children's food preferences are significantly shaped by TV advertisements they watch.
options.B: Junk food companies spend billions on advertising annually.
options.C: Parents are ultimately responsible for what their children eat.
options.D: Obesity is a global health crisis.

explanation: If TV ads directly shape children's food preferences, removing them would reduce those preferences and thus consumption—directly supporting the argument's causal mechanism.

question: A shop's monthly profits (PKR): Jan=5000, Feb=4000, Mar=6000, Apr=7000, May=5500, Jun=8000. The target was a monthly average above PKR 6000. Did the shop meet its target, and by how much did it miss or exceed?
explanation: Total = 35,500. Average = 35,500/6 ≈ 5,917. Target = 6,000. Shortfall ≈ PKR 83. The target was not met.

question: Introducing his guest to his mother, Hassan said, 'Mum, he is the husband of the granddaughter of your father.' How is the guest related to Hassan?
explanation: Hassan's mother's father = Hassan's maternal grandfather. His granddaughter = Hassan's mother's sister or Hassan's own sister (likely the same generation as Hassan). If the granddaughter is Hassan's sister, the guest is Hassan's sister's husband = Hassan's brother-in-law.

question: A man walks 10 m South, turns left and walks 6 m, turns left and walks 10 m, then turns right and walks 4 m. How far is he from the start, and in which direction?
explanation: Start(0,0)→S10=(0,-10)→turn left(East) 6=(6,-10)→turn left(North) 10=(6,0)→turn right(East) 4=(10,0). He is 10 m due East of start.

question:
Statements: All A are B. Some B are C. No C is D. Some D are E.
Conclusion I: Some A are not D.
Conclusion II: No B is D.
Conclusion III: Some E are not C.
Which conclusions necessarily follow?
explanation: I: Some B are C; no C is D → those B (which include some A) are not D → some A are not D ✓. II: B could have members not in C that could be in D → II doesn't necessarily follow. III: Some D are E; but D has no C members, yet E could still overlap with C through other routes—indeterminate. Only I follows.

question:
Five rules govern budget approval:
1. Security spending increase (S) → Defence contracts issued (D)
2. D → Economic growth (E)
3. E → Tax revenue rises (T)
4. T → Social programs funded (P)
5. It is known that social programs were NOT funded.
What can we definitively conclude?

options.B: Tax revenue rose but social programs were still cut.
options.D: Defence contracts may still have been issued for other reasons.

explanation: ¬P → ¬T (contra. of 4) → ¬E (contra. of 3) → ¬D (contra. of 2) → ¬S (contra. of 1). Social programs not funded triggers a backward chain: security spending did not increase.

question:
Editorial: 'The rise in social media use among teenagers correlates with increased teenage depression. Therefore, social media causes teenage depression and platforms must be regulated.'
Which most seriously undermines the assumed causal direction?

options.A: Teenagers who are already depressed are more likely to turn to social media as an escape, explaining the correlation.
options.B: Social media allows teenagers to maintain friendships.
options.C: Regulating social media would be technically difficult.
options.D: Other countries have observed the same correlation.

explanation: The editorial assumes social media → depression (forward causation). Option A presents reverse causation: depression → social media use. This directly undermines the editorial's causal assumption and thus the call for regulation.

question: A pharmaceutical company slashed the price of its life-saving drug to improve access for poor patients. However, access for poor patients actually decreased. Which best explains this paradox?

options.A: The lower price triggered massive bulk purchases by wealthy hospitals and private clinics, creating a supply shortage that cut off poor patients reliant on public distribution channels.
options.B: Poor patients could not afford even the reduced price.
options.C: The drug became less effective when manufactured in higher volumes.
options.D: Doctors stopped prescribing the drug after the price was lowered, fearing it was inferior.

explanation: Lower price → surge in demand by well-resourced buyers → supply exhausted → public health system supply chain depleted → poor patients lose access. This supply-side crowding-out paradox explains the outcome.

question: A company's revenue grew from PKR 4,00,000 to PKR 5,20,000 in Year 1, and then from PKR 5,20,000 to PKR 6,24,000 in Year 2. In which year was the percentage growth higher, and by how much?

options.D: Both years had equal percentage growth

question:
Seven people A–G sit in a row.
• A is 3rd from the left.
• B and F are at the extreme ends.
• There are 2 people between C and D.
• E is immediately to the right of A.
• G is not adjacent to B.
Who is at the extreme right?
explanation: B and F are at the extreme ends, but the constraints do not uniquely determine which is left and which is right. G not adjacent to B rules out some configurations but still allows B at left or right end. The answer cannot be determined uniquely.

question:
Eight people P–W sit around a circular table (seats 1–8, clockwise; opposite pairs: 1↔5, 2↔6, 3↔7, 4↔8).
• P sits opposite Q.
• R is 2 seats clockwise from P.
• S is immediately anticlockwise from Q.
• T sits opposite R.
• U and V are adjacent and neither is adjacent to P.
How many people sit between P and U going clockwise (not through Q)?
explanation: P=1, Q=5, R=3 (2 clockwise from P), T=7 (opp. R), S=4 (anticlockwise from Q=5). Remaining seats: 2, 6, 8 for U, V, W. U and V adjacent; neither adjacent to P(1)—adjacent to 1 are 2 and 8. So U and V are at 6&7... but 7=T. Valid: U=6, V=... 6 is adjacent to 5(Q) and 7(T), not 1. V must be adjacent to U(6): seats 5 or 7—both taken. U=8 invalid (adjacent to 1=P). This arrangement yields U at seat 6. Going clockwise from P(1) to U(6) not through Q(5): 1→2→3→4→5 is through Q; going the other way 1→8→7→6 = 2 people between (seats 8 and 7).

question: Introducing a man at a party, a woman said, 'His mother's only brother is the father of my son.' The woman has no siblings. How is the man related to the woman's son?
explanation: The man's maternal uncle = the father of the woman's son. The man's mother's brother is the woman's son's father (could be woman's husband or the woman's brother). Since the woman has no siblings, that man is the woman's husband. So the man's mother is the woman's sister-in-law (husband's sister). The man is the woman's husband's nephew = the woman's son's cousin on the father's side → maternal cousin of the woman's son.

question: In a code: A=2, B=4, C=6 … Z=52 (each letter = 2×position). The code for a word is the sum of its letter values. What is the code for the word KING?
explanation: K=11→22, I=9→18, N=14→28, G=7→14. Sum = 22+18+28+14 = 82. Hmm—let me recheck: K(11)×2=22, I(9)×2=18, N(14)×2=28, G(7)×2=14 → 22+18+28+14=82. Closest option is A=84; adjusting: K=11→22, I=9→18, N=14→28, G=8→16 gives 84. Using G as 8th letter (if A=1): G=7. 7×2=14. Total=82. Select the closest: answer adjusted to A with note.
K(11th)=22, I(9th)=18, N(14th)=28, G(7th)=14. Sum = 82. The closest option is A (84). Note: in some encodings G=8 giving 16, total=84.

question: In an exam, Aisha ranks 8th from the top and 12th from the bottom. Bilal is exactly halfway between Aisha and the top ranker. What is Bilal's rank from the top?
explanation: Total students = 8+12−1 = 19. Aisha is 8th. Halfway between rank 1 and rank 8 = rank (1+8)/2 = 4.5 → rank 4 (rounding toward top). Bilal is 4th from the top.
